text: On Tulving's account, the 'autonoetic consciousness' that distinguishes episodic memory refers to which of the following?
choices: Awareness of impersonal general facts about the world (noetic consciousness)
The immediate, non-thematic retention of a just-past note
The self-referential awareness of re-experiencing one's own past in subjective time
Procedural, non-conscious knowledge of how to perform a skill
explanation: Autonoetic consciousness is the self-referential awareness of re-experiencing one's own past in subjective time ('mental time travel'), which Tulving takes to be constitutive of episodic memory. Awareness of impersonal facts is merely noetic consciousness (semantic memory); retention of a just-past note is Husserl's category; and procedural know-how lacks experiential self-reference altogether.
